coverage: Global developments from 30 October to 6 November 2026
summary: This week brought two verifiable application advances on the quantum-energy side. In Europe, IQM and Volkswagen Group Innovation applied quantum-classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) to chemistry relevant to lithium-air batteries, with classical post-processing sped up by up to about 124 times on a 50-orbital benchmark, and validated the work on IQM's Emerald hardware. In China, a Shenzhen-Hong Kong team embedded a domestic coherent photonic quantum computer in a Guangdong power-market simulation, cutting mean absolute error on back-tests by more than 20% versus conventional methods. On the fusion side, the US Department of Energy's INFUSE programme announced $8.5 million for 28 public-private projects, and several fusion companies signed supply-chain MoUs around a Japan-Germany summit (including Fujikura high-temperature superconducting tape and laser-fusion cooperation). On the RWA side, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority took the Ensemble TX pilot to 24/7 interbank settlement in tokenised central-bank money, and the SFC said at FinTech Week that the focus was shifting "from laying tracks to generating traffic"; Switzerland's SEALSQ and Eco Wave Power demonstrated a trusted digital twin of renewable generation and automated trading; tokenised ETF/ETP assets were about $687 million as of 2 November.
trends: Quantum-energy applications have extended from grid-optimisation experiments on real hardware to battery chemistry and power-market decisions: IQM × Volkswagen reports a maximum ~124-fold speed-up in classical post-processing on 50 orbitals, with validation on Emerald hardware; the Shenzhen-Hong Kong team cut back-test error in the Guangdong power market by more than 20% and stresses that the evidence is traceable.

Fusion competition continues to centre on supply chains and public-private interfaces: US INFUSE is connecting 22 companies with national laboratories through $8.5 million and 28 small awards; the Japan-Germany summit wrote HTS tape, laser fusion and the tritium cycle into several MoUs.

RWA regulation and settlement were upgraded in Hong Kong on the same day: 24/7 interbank settlement in tokenised central-bank money, plus an SFC narrative that "the tracks are laid, now comes traffic". There are 17 tokenised retail products with about $1.3 billion in AUM.

The scale of tokenised assets is still skewed toward standardised financial products: tokenised ETF/ETPs were about $687 million as of 2 November, far smaller than the on-chain distributed RWA total cited in last week's brief. This week's only energy real-asset RWA was a demonstration-level trusted-trading exercise by SEALSQ × Eco Wave, not yet large-scale settlement.

No new rules specifically on energy RWAs were issued this week by FINMA, the EU's MiCA/ESMA or the China Securities Regulatory Commission. The main moves were in Hong Kong's Ensemble/SFC work and US market infrastructure.
footer: All facts and figures in this brief are taken from the public sources listed. The IQM/Volkswagen results include technical research at preprint or white-paper level; the SEALSQ/Eco Wave work is a concept demonstration and is explicitly not a completed settlement; INFUSE selections remain subject to negotiation of awards. The original texts prevail. Time window: 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-06 (Zurich time). This edition has no new peer-reviewed Nature/Science-level energy papers or annual reports requiring permanent archiving, and no permanent record was created.

items.title: IQM × Volkswagen: QC-AFQMC speeds up simulation of next-generation battery chemistry, with up to about 124-fold acceleration on a 50-orbital benchmark
items.what: According to Quantum Computing Report on 5 November, European quantum-hardware company IQM and Volkswagen Group Innovation, in a technical study titled "Quantum-Classical Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo at the Edge of Practicability", applied quantum-classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) to strongly correlated electronic-structure problems. Using an Aitken block transformation and automatic differentiation, the team cut the complexity of each classical post-processing step from about Õ(N^5.5) to Õ(N^4.5). On a 50-orbital benchmark, classical solve time was shortened by up to about 124 times (an estimated ~248 times at 100 orbitals). For hardware validation, they completed a stretched H₈ ground-state calculation on IQM's commercial Emerald superconducting processor (with MPS tensor-network error filtering), and used a 40-qubit active space to simulate a Li₂O₄ lithium-peroxide dimer rearrangement (26 electrons / 20 orbitals), a path related to intermediate states in lithium-air battery charge and discharge. IQM's case page and a white-paper abstract were released at the same time.
items.why: Battery materials are an area where quantum computing is often promised and seldom given a checkable industrial benchmark. This week's results set out the speed-up, orbital scale, hardware validation and specific chemical system clearly, while also acknowledging that significant runtime challenges remain before practical use. They make a useful yardstick for assessing similar collaborations.
items.src: Quantum Computing Report / IQM Case Study

items.title: A Shenzhen-Hong Kong "quantum-AI power-market simulation system" is deployed in Guangdong: back-test error more than 20% lower than conventional methods
items.what: The China Securities Journal's CNStock reported on 1 November that a quantum-AI-based power-market simulation and intelligent-assessment system jointly developed by the Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, the China Southern Power Grid Energy Development Research Institute and the QuantumMind team at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, had made progress. The system follows a path of "quantum computing + large language models + specialist numerical models": quantum AI (QART running on a domestic Boson Quantum coherent photonic quantum computer) does global search among a large number of model-collaboration schemes, then dispatches large models and numerical models to execute; each forecast comes with data grounds, original evidence and a reviewable analysis trail. Back-tests show that, in the Guangdong power market, mean absolute forecast error was more than 20% lower than conventional methods the team had actually used, including ARIMA, LSTM and XGBoost, covering load, prices, spreads and information assessment. The platform ingests more than 200,000 industry and policy items a day; the structured rate of useful information rose by more than 15% relatively, and recall of core events by more than 10% relatively.
items.why: Unlike last week's Hefei focus on quantum-encrypted dispatch and precision measurement, this week's China case embeds quantum computing directly in power-market forecasting and trusted assessment, and gives a checkable error comparison — new evidence of "quantum + energy" landing on the trading side.

items.title: HKMA Ensemble TX upgraded to 24/7 settlement in tokenised central-bank money; SFC at FinTech Week calls for a shift "from tracks to traffic"
items.what: On 2 November the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced that Ensemble TX, in the pilot phase of Project Ensemble, had entered a new stage: supporting 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenised-deposit transactions with tokenised central-bank money (tokenised CeBM). Participating banks have risen to 12 and industry pioneers to 20. HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said Ensemble had moved from experiment toward commercialisation within two years. The same day, Christina Choi, Executive Director of the SFC's Investment Products Division, gave a keynote at Hong Kong FinTech Week titled "From Tracks to Traffic": 17 authorised tokenised retail products (money-market funds, gold products, ETFs and others) with about $1.3 billion in assets under management; last week the first tokenised public money-market funds were approved for secondary trading on licensed platforms; the next priorities are secondary trading and treasury management, with a tokenised gold ETF pilot also under consideration; and an "innovation pathway" will offer regulatory flexibility for controlled pilots. Both the HKMA and the SFC stressed that they would continue to coordinate.
items.why: Advancing the settlement layer (tokenised central-bank money, 24/7) and the product layer (secondary trading of tokenised funds) on the same day is a key step in taking Hong Kong tokenisation from "can be issued" to "can trade continuously and settle across institutions", and it has demonstrative value as a compliance channel for green and energy RWAs.
items.src: Hong Kong Monetary Authority press release / Hong Kong SFC speech

items.title: US Department of Energy INFUSE: $8.5 million for 28 public-private fusion projects, covering 22 companies
items.what: On 2 November the US Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science announced that, through the Innovation Network for Fusion Energy (INFUSE) programme, it would put $8.5 million in fiscal year 2026 into 28 awards connecting US private fusion companies with DOE national laboratories and universities. Seventeen are led by national laboratories and 11 by universities, involving 22 different commercial firms. Individual budgets are about $100,000 to $500,000, for one to two years, managed after peer review under the lead of Oak Ridge, Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory and Lawrence Livermore, among others. Projects focus on modelling and simulation, materials science, plasma diagnostics and enabling technologies. DOE has also opened applications for fiscal year 2027 assistance, adding consortium eligibility and a pre-conceptual design review theme for fusion demonstration plants. Officials note that selection for negotiation is not a commitment to fund.
items.why: Relative to last week's large CHIPS Act semiconductor awards to Helion and CFS, INFUSE is smaller and more about joint laboratory-company work, showing that the United States is keeping a dispersed, reviewable research interface alongside large industrial subsidies.
items.src: US Department of Energy Office of Science

items.title: Multiple fusion MoUs around a Japan-Germany summit: Proxima × Fujikura to assess an HTS-tape plant in Germany; Focused Energy expands laser-fusion cooperation
items.what: The American Nuclear Society's Nuclear Newswire summarised on 3 November that, during German Chancellor Merz's visit to Japan, the two leaders issued a joint statement on advanced-technology cooperation, pledging collaboration in stellarators and laser fusion, among other areas; several companies signed cooperation documents around the same day. Besides the Proxima Fusion × Kyoto Fusioneering MoU already reported last week (gyrotrons and the fuel cycle), new points include: Proxima and Japan's Fujikura signed an MoU to assess the technical, commercial and economic feasibility of an industrial-scale high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape manufacturing base in Germany (especially Lower Saxony); Focused Energy (a German-US laser inertial-fusion firm) and Kyoto Fusioneering signed an MoU covering fuel/targets, the tritium cycle, materials for extreme environments and diagnostics; the Institute of Laser Engineering at Osaka University and Focused Energy signed an MoU covering laser design, ignition concepts and diagnostics; Mitsui & Co., Kyoto Fusioneering and Siemens Energy signed an MoU; and Helical Fusion and Gauss Fusion issued a joint statement of intent to cooperate. Germany had already established three fusion hubs, for lasers, magnetic confinement (stellarators) and the fuel cycle/materials.
items.why: The competitive focus continues to shift from who first produces a device to who first builds a manufacturable supply chain. HTS tape is a key bottleneck for stellarator magnets, and the Fujikura cooperation puts the supply-chain question at the level of an industrial feasibility study.
items.src: ANS Nuclear Newswire (summary of agreements around the Japan-Germany summit)

items.title: SEALSQ × Eco Wave Power: a three-year MoU and a demonstration of a trusted digital twin of wave energy and auditable automated trading
items.what: Geneva-based SEALSQ (Nasdaq: LAES) announced on 5 November a three-year memorandum of understanding with its parent WISeQey, sister company SEALCOIN AG and Eco Wave Power's US subsidiary, and the completion of two capability demonstrations at a wave-energy installation in Jaffa Port, Israel: (1) a trusted digital twin — connecting physical generation to a digital representation with verifiable origin and integrity; and (2) certified automated trading — using trusted production data to initiate secure, authorised, auditable trades under predefined commercial conditions. The cooperation is aimed at potential buyers including AI data centres, industrial users, aggregators and utilities, and plans to explore the SEALSQ QS7001 post-quantum secure element and post-quantum cryptography. The press release states clearly that the demonstration does not constitute a physical power-purchase agreement or a completed funds settlement, and that future deployment still depends on technical validation, applicable regulation and separate commercial agreements. The results are to be shown live at Quantum Days 2026 in Cannes on 19 November.
items.why: Stringing "renewable physical output → trusted data → automated trading" into a demonstrable closed loop, with an explicit post-quantum security path, is one of the few public models on the energy side that approaches RWA or machine-to-machine trading. The company also discloses of its own accord that settlement has not taken place, reducing the risk of over-interpretation.

items.title: Wall Street's tokenisation model takes shape: DTCC keeps expanding; tokenised ETF/ETPs about $687 million as of 2 November
items.what: The Block's Tokenization Briefing on 5 November noted that, after DTCC's tokenization service went live on 28 October, 20 DTC participant firms (including JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity and Bank of America) had joined, connecting to Canton and DTCC's private chain, with plans to add other chains in 2027. NYSE/ICE is advancing a tokenised trading platform. Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate have joined Securitize and tZERO as transfer agents; three of the traditional transfer agents serve nearly 5,000 listed companies, about 99% of the S&P 500. Tokenised ETF/ETPs have grown from about $164 million at the end of 2025 to about $687 million on 2 November 2026; BNB Chain, at about $309 million, has overtaken Ethereum at about $229.2 million as the largest chain for this asset class. The article also notes that most tokenisation-themed stocks have underperformed bitcoin since Securitize's listing, a sign of a phase with many announcements and little revenue.
items.why: Infrastructure (custody, transfer, exchanges) and product structure (ETFs ahead of single-stock tokens) are becoming clearer at the same time. The scale data show that RWA growth is still concentrated in standardised financial products, not in energy real assets themselves.
